items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: It was Bonnie Bigaud playing with him at the time that he took me right off.

ctx.x: Did you begin to work with this band on a regular basis? Who was that on the band on? Yeah.

Well, after, when the fellows would see me coming on a job, a guy would send me pretty often, you know? And when they'd see me coming on a job, I could see that they wasn't satisfied. Uh-huh. But he sent me so often and I would practice so hard, you know, to do better every time I'd go. So, oh my. Bernard asked me one night, he said, look, you want to belong to my band? Yeah. I said, well, sorry, me if the fellows are satisfied. I said, uh, you know, you got this other band. He said, that's all right. If you can…
Was he playing clarinet then or saxophone? He said clarinet. When did he take up saxophone, do you know? No, I don't. Well, what was the next band after that that you played with?
